entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

description.description: New description for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 14400000 ms, max 28800000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 28800000ms / 480 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 14400000ms (240 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 28800000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 14400000 ms, max 28800000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskCreate
tools.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

description.description: What needs to be done

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

tools.name: TaskUpdate
tools.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

description.description: New description for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_target_open

Takes effect only in Deep mode (Ghidra); it lets Deep target processors the built-in
clean-room engine doesn't cover, and overrides the `ghidra.language_id` setting for this
target. Ignored in Clean room.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bytes_find
tools.description: Find every place a byte signature or a piece of text occurs in a file (an absolute path, or the active target). `pattern` is hex byte pairs with `??` for any byte (spaces optional, e.g. `48 8B ?? 24`); `text` is searched as UTF-8 and/or UTF-16LE. Matches are ordered by file offset and paged (offset/limit); for ELF, PE and Mach-O programs each match also carries its virtual address and containing section when the bytes are mapped. Overlapping matches are all reported. Counting stops at 100000 matches.

document.description: Open document (id or name) to search instead of the active one; ignored with path.

encoding.description: How `text` is encoded in the file: utf8, utf16le or both (default).

path.description: Absolute path of the file to search; the active target when omitted.

pattern.description: Hex byte pairs with `??` wildcards, e.g. "48 8B ?? 24 ?? 00".

oneOf.description: Both UTF-8 and UTF-16LE (default).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.description: Structured pseudo-C from the built-in clean-room lifter: register-level variables, if/else and loops from the control-flow graph, resolved call names, inline string literals. Honest about its limits.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

function.description: Function name or address (0x-hex; any address inside it works).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_pe_resources_list
tools.description: PE32/PE32+ resource tree (type → name → language) with SHA-256 of each item, icon groups, version information and the manifest. Built-in parser. Uses the active target unless path is given.

max_file_bytes.description: Refuse files bigger than this (64 MiB..512 MiB, default 64 MiB).

path.description: Absolute path of a PE file; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_strings_find
tools.description: Complete, deterministic search of the program's strings. mode literal or regex; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: What to look for.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_xrefs_list
tools.description: References to an address (calls, jumps, data, strings, pointers, imports) and the references made from it. Defaults to the cursor. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_check
tools.description: For the builder: test the project's current build against the original now, with the same checks Craft Anything runs after each turn (a website's likeness at each width with the padding, colour, font and layout differences; an app's or game's picture against the original's; whether it builds; the mechanics sheet; credits). The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it lists and check again before replying. Not counted as a round. project defaults to the project this tool server works for.

project.description: The project's folder; default: the project this tool server was started for.

wait_minutes.description:
Longest wait for the result, in minutes (1..=60, default 20): a website with several pages
or a game's engine build takes a few minutes.

# Mechanics sheet — modern rebuild of the 1999 word processor

Everything here was read from the original program (`wordpro.exe`, its English
language library `wpenc70.dll`, and its data files) or measured from the
captured window. Values marked **estimated** were looked for and not found.

## Menus (wpenc70.dll, extended menu resource 1002)

Top level, in order: File, Edit, View, Create, Page, Text, Window, Help
(the screenshot shows exactly these for an empty document; Frame / Table /
Columns only appear when such an object is selected).

Kept (modernised):
- File: New Document (101), Open… Ctrl+O (790), Close (147), Save Ctrl+S (103),
  Save As… (104), Import/Export… (152) → Export as Rich Text / Plain Text,
  Print… (111) → not available yet, Document Properties (1629), User Setup →
  Preferences (162), SmartCorrect Setup (1505), Exit (113), Last Open Files (2094).
- Edit: Undo Ctrl+Z (151), Redo (156, "Undo/Redo Special"), Cut/Copy/Paste
  (153/154/155), Go To… Ctrl+G (452), Find & Replace Text… Ctrl+F (451),
  Proofing Tools → Word Count (1974), Select All.
- View: Layout (210), Draft (211), Full Page (201), Standard 100% (203),
  Zoom To → Margin Width (778), Page Width (779), 75% (796), 150% (797),
  200% (204), Other… (1673); Show/Hide → SmartIcons (208), Status Bar (265),
  Ruler (207), Headers & Footers (775), Clean Screen (233), marks.
- Create: Page break, Date/Time, Symbol, Bulleted / numbered list,
  Footnote-style "Comment note" left out.
- Page: Page Properties (381), Page Size, Margins, Orientation, Background,
  Header, Footer, Insert Page Number (356), Insert Page Break Ctrl+Enter (358).
- Text: Font & Color (251), Bullets & Numbers (285), Named Styles (1633),
  Normal (253), Attributes Bold Ctrl+B / Italic Ctrl+I / Underline Ctrl+U
  (254/255/256), Enlarge Text F4 (252), Reduce Text Shift+F4 (245),
  Alignment Left Ctrl+L / Center Ctrl+E / Right Ctrl+R / Full Justify Ctrl+J
  (259–262), Indent (258) / Outdent (284), Insert Other → Date/Time (158),
  Symbol (1973); case change from cmddefs (ToggleAllUpper 128 / ToggleAllLower 129),
  Highlight (cmddefs HighLight 143), Strikethrough (ToggleStrikeThru 127),
  Superscript/Subscript (103/104).
- Window: New Window, Close Window, Close All → documents become tabs.
- Help: Keyboard shortcuts, About.

Removed on request (no scanning, no internet, no sharing):
TWAIN Image → Acquire Image / Select Source (2116/2113/2115, `TWAIN_32.DLL`
at 0x8ac708), TeamMail (1637), TeamReview (602), TeamConsolidate (500),
TeamSecurity (600), Internet submenu (1957: HTML export, open/save to
internet, web tools, setup), Hyperlink (1935), InfoBus data link (883),
Show/Hide Internet Tools (1979), Lotus Internet Support (1616), Year 2000 (556).
The rebuild makes no network connections at all.

## Defaults

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Default font | Times New Roman | status bar in capture; fallback rule FUN_0058ac4f; the person confirmed |
| Default size | 12 pt | status bar in capture; the person confirmed |
| Default paragraph style name | "Default Text" | status bar in capture |
| Font fallback | fixed pitch → Courier New; swiss family (0x20) → Arial; otherwise → Times New Roman | FUN_0058ac4f (0x58ac4f) |
| New document name | "Untitled" + counter in base 10 → "Untitled1" | FUN_0044e7a6 (0x44e7a6) with string 6053 |
| Page indicator | " Pg %d", only redrawn when the page changes | FUN_00452923 (0x452923) with string 6049 |
| Page number text | "Page %d" | string 10678 |
| Word count message | "The document contains %ld characters and %ld words." / "The selected text contains …" | strings 15723/15724 |
| Find options | Whole words only, Words starting with, Words ending with, Words containing | strings 10916–10919 |
| Find scope | Entire document | string 10929 |
| Units | Inches (in) / Points (pts) | strings 10766 / 10769 |
| Page size | 8.5 × 11 in (Letter) | measured: page 1004 px wide, margins 118/120 px → 8.5 in with 1 in margins |
| Margins | 1 in all round | measured from capture (estimated for top/bottom) |
| Zoom start | 100 % ("Standard (100%)") | menu 203; the person: always start at 100 % |
| Zoom range | 25 % – 200 % | the person's decision |
| Zoom presets | Margin Width, Page Width, 75 %, 100 %, 150 %, 200 %, Full Page | menu 1630 |
| SmartCorrect list | 170 English pairs (e.g. teh→the, 1/2→½) | `ltscorrt.reg`, key SmartCorrect\2.0\en |
| Timed save | on, every 10 minutes | command TimeSave (cmddefs 12); interval **estimated** |
| Undo depth | 100 steps | **estimated** |
| Enlarge / Reduce step | 2 pt (min 6, max 96) | **estimated** (no table found, unknown unk_44f0eda0475d11cd) |
| Font size list | 8 9 10 11 12 14 16 18 20 24 28 32 36 48 72 | **estimated** |

- Tabs instead of MDI child windows; Ctrl+N new document (original Ctrl+N was "Normal";
  Normal moved to Ctrl+Space).
- Flat, line-style toolbar icons drawn as vector shapes; light and dark themes.
- Live word count and page count in the status bar; zoom slider.
- Redo (Ctrl+Y), Find & Replace with live match count, match case.
- Documents saved in a local `.wpx` file (JSON) on this computer only; export to RTF and TXT; text files open.

- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskCreate
tools.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

description.description: What needs to be done

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

tools.name: TaskUpdate
tools.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

description.description: New description for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

content.text:
I've built a new standalone version of the word processor. It never connects to the internet and has no scanning (TWAIN) or sharing features. The build succeeds, Craft Anything's comparison check now passes, and six automatic tests of typing and page layout pass. I also looked at a sample document on screen to confirm the text draws correctly.

**What's in it:**
- The original's menu order (File, Edit, View, Create, Page, Text, Window, Help), with all the internet, scanning and team-sharing commands taken out.
- A single row of new flat, modern icons.
- Documents open in tabs instead of separate windows.
- Real pages with margins, a ruler, headers and footers, and page numbers.
- Text styles, fonts, colours, highlighting, alignment, bullets and numbering.
- Find & Replace with the original's four match options (whole words, starting with, ending with, containing), plus a word count.
- The original's own list of 170 auto-corrections (for example "teh" becomes "the").
- A recovery copy saved every 10 minutes, kept only on this computer.
- Light and dark themes.

As you asked, it always opens at 100% zoom, lets you zoom from 25% to 200%, and starts in 12-point Times New Roman.

**What's different or missing:**
- **Name:** it's called "Scribe Pro". The question about using the "Word Pro" name got no answer, and that name is a trademark.
- **Printing and spell checking aren't included yet.** For now you can save as Rich Text and print from another program.
- **Old files:** it saves its own document files and Rich Text or plain text files, but can't open the old program's own document files. Save those as Rich Text in the old program first.
- **Estimated details:** I couldn't find the original's exact list of font sizes, or how much F4 grows text, so those are my best guesses.

A good next request would be "add printing and a spell checker that works offline".

definition.description: For an APK (or one Flutter library): which ABIs ship libapp.so/libflutter.so, the Dart snapshot version hash (null with candidates when libraries disagree), Dart versions and toolchains the binaries state, GNU build ids, and the size and SHA-256 of each libflutter.so. Built-in parser.

path.description: Absolute path of an APK (or a libapp.so / libflutter.so); the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_decompile
definition.description: Ask JEB to decompile one type or method (upstream decompile_code_item) by item_address, optionally inside unit_path. The output is JEB's, recorded as external evidence.

item_address.description: The item's address in JEB's notation, e.g. `Lcom/example/Main;` or `Lcom/example/Main;->onCreate(Landroid/os/Bundle;)V`.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

unit_path.description: The code unit holding the item; JEB's default when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_open
definition.description: Ask the user-run JEB MCP server to open an absolute file path as a project (upstream open_project). Not idempotent: JEB keeps the project open.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to open in JEB (APK, DEX, ...).

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_units_browse
definition.description: List the units of the open JEB project (upstream list_units), optionally under parent_unit_path and filtered, one page at a time (index, count ≤ 100).

filter.description: Only units whose name or path matches this text.

parent_unit_path.description: List the children of this unit instead of the project's top-level units.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_method_show
definition.description: A method's Dalvik bytecode as a smali-like listing with registers, resolved strings, types, fields and methods, branch targets, switch and array payloads and try/catch handlers (built-in decoder). With java_source=true and JADX installed, also attaches JADX's Java decompilation of the class.

java_source.description: Also ask JADX (if installed) for Java source of the class. Default false.

overload_index.description: Which overload (0-based, in declaration order) when the name is overloaded; 0 when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_package_show
definition.description: Read an APK with built-in parsers: the manifest (package, versions, SDK levels, permissions, components with exported state and intent filters, application flags) decoded from binary XML, signing certificates (v1 PKCS#7 files and the v2/v3 signing block; signatures and content digests are verified, but not whether the certificate is one you trust), DEX files and native libraries per ABI.

include_manifest_xml.description: Include the decoded manifest as XML text (default true).

path.description: Absolute path of the APK; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_resources_read
definition.description: Decode resources.arsc with the built-in parser: packages, resource types and their configurations (locale, density, night mode, SDK...), every entry with typed values and style bags, string resources per locale; optionally decode compiled res/*.xml files to text. Paged.

locale.description: Only this locale (`fr`, `es-rMX`; `default` for the unqualified one).

only_locales.description: Only these locales, each with its own string table (`["de", "fr", "default"]`); adds to `locale`.

path.description: Absolute path of the APK or a resources.arsc file; the active target when omitted.

type_name.description: Only entries of this resource type (`string`, `color`, `style`...).

with_strings.description: Include string resources grouped by locale (default true).

xml_files.description: Compiled XML files inside the APK to decode to text (e.g. `res/layout/main.xml`), at most 16.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_builds_line_up
definition.description: Pair the functions of two builds of a program (two absolute paths) with the built-in engine. In order: unique names that aren't generated; identical bytes; bytes with addresses masked out; a structural fingerprint of block count, called names and referenced strings. Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as changed when its code differs. Candidates that can't be told apart stay unpaired and are listed as ambiguous. Lists are paged together (offset/limit); show picks one; detail=summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse. Nothing is executed. Takes as long as analysing both programs.

detail.description: complete (default) returns the page; summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse.

left.description: Absolute path of the first (older) build.

max_file_bytes.description: Refuse files bigger than this (up to 2 GiB, default 512 MiB).

right.description: Absolute path of the second (newer) build.

show.description: all (default), pairs, changed (pairs whose code differs), ambiguous, only_left or only_right.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

MatchShow.description: Which list of a match to return.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_call_path_find
definition.description: Find a path of calls from a start address to a goal address over a call graph assembled from native_function_study evidence records.

functions.description: native_function_study evidence records that describe the functions and their callees.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_changes_summarize
definition.description: Combine several comparison evidence records (app_function_versions_compare, core_archives_compare, runtime_captures_compare) into one summary of what changed and what stayed the same.

comparisons.description:
One or more comparison evidence records (app_function_versions_compare / core_archives_compare /
runtime_captures_compare / core_evidence_exports_compare), inline or by reference.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_coverage_evaluate
definition.description: Summarise a rebuild ledger: the share of in-scope expectations proven, counts by layer and status, and the open gaps with what each still needs.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_feature_follow
definition.description: Follow a feature through an application graph from a seed (module, function, string, IPC channel, endpoint, route, bridge API or node id): what leads to it and what it leads to, across renderer ↔ preload ↔ main, with readable chains and a one-line story.

application.description: js_app_map evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) or an absolute path to analyse.

oneOf.description: What the seed leads to.
What leads to the seed.
Case-insensitive substring.

value.description: What to look for: a channel name, function name, string, module path, URL fragment or node id.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_folder_explain
definition.description: Survey an installed app's folder (absolute path; a macOS .app or its Contents, a Windows or Linux install folder) when you don't know what it is. Walks the folder within max_entries and max_depth, following no links, running nothing and writing nothing, and reads only the first and last 4 KiB of the files that need a look, plus a search of up to 64 MiB of up to 4 main programs for Tauri's own text, to name the runtimes it may be built on: Electron, Tauri, CEF, Qt, Flutter, .NET, Java, Python (with PyInstaller), Node, Unity, Unreal, Godot, other game engines, or plain native code. Each candidate has a strength and the files that support it, and next_steps says which tool to run on which file. These are inferences: a file being there doesn't prove the app runs it.

max_depth.description: How many folders deep to look (up to 32).

max_entries.description: Most files and folders to look at (up to 200000).

path.description: Absolute path of the installed app's folder.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_function_versions_compare
definition.description: Compare two native_function_study evidence records: name, size, blocks, instructions, callee set and pseudo-code. Reports what changed.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_graphs_compare
definition.description: Compare two application graphs: modules (unchanged, changed, moved by content, renamed by structure, added, removed), bundle modules (content → structure → id), IPC channels and handlers, bridge members, endpoints, routes, window webPreferences, native modules and vendor versions.

left.description: The older version: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer version, in the same forms.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_ledger_build
definition.description: Derive the expectations a clean-room rebuild must meet from an application graph (IPC handlers, bridge members, windows, endpoints, routes, storage, file/process effects, native modules, entry point) and mark each one proven only when the manifest gives it one owner, a parser type where needed, every case it must cover with strong enough evidence, and a passing check with its result. Ledger status: ready, open, failing or unclear.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

manifest.description: How the rebuild binds expectations to owners, cases and verifiers.

reviewed_expectations.description: Expectations reviewed as out of scope or blocked.

kind.description: works, refuses, bad-input, cancel or shutdown.

strength.description: unit-test, module-test, network-test, page-test, built-app, native-call, live-run or outside-check.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_rebuild_claim_check
definition.description: Check a reconstruction specification: every expectation must cite evidence that exists and is intact. Reports which expectations are satisfied.

expectations.description: Each expectation must be backed by evidence that exists and is intact.

goal.description: What is claimed to have been reconstructed.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_runtime_correlate
definition.description: Correlate static comparisons (app_function_versions_compare/core_archives_compare) with runtime comparisons (runtime_captures_compare) through caller-supplied mappings, and report where they agree or disagree.

mappings.description: Each mapping links a static record to a runtime record by their evidence ids.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_source_import
definition.description: Read a reference source tree (honouring .gitignore, skipping .git and hidden files) into a source graph: every file with sha256 and language; JavaScript/TypeScript files with exports, imports, function names, strings and a structural fingerprint. Use with js_source_bundle_compare.

include_hidden.description: Include dot-files and dot-folders (other than .git, always skipped).

path.description: Absolute path of the source folder.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_app_graph_build
definition.description: Project an iOS/macOS app's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: bundles and extensions, executables, frameworks, dylibs, signing material, interface files, asset catalogs and embedded runtimes (Flutter, React Native, Electron, Unity...). Runtime hints are inferred from file names.

inventory.description: core_archive_show evidence (inline or retained). Its recorded path is re-read for the full inventory.

path.description: Or an absolute path to inventory now. Defaults to the active target when neither is given.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_archive_decode
definition.description: Read an NSKeyedArchiver property list: archiver, $top entries, the object table (paged) and the object graph below a root with references resolved (cycles and repeats become $ref).

offset.description: First row of the object table page.

path.description: Absolute path of the archive; the active target when omitted.

root.description: $top entry to project (default: "root", else the first).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_assets_list
definition.description: Read a compiled asset catalog (Assets.car): BOM blocks and variables, catalog header, key format, facet names, appearances and a page of renditions (name, size, scale, pixel format, layout). Image pixels are not decoded.

path.description: Absolute path of Assets.car or an app bundle containing one; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_calls_observe
definition.description: Launch a macOS program under lldb, set breakpoints on named functions and ObjC selectors, and record each hit with its argument registers. Bounded by duration and event count. macOS only.

duration_ms.description: How long to let it run, in milliseconds (100..=600000).

executable.description: Absolute path to the macOS program to launch under the debugger.

oneOf.description: Break when a named function is entered.
Break on an Objective-C method.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_dispatch_show
definition.description: Objective-C method dispatch (class, selector, implementation) and Swift dispatch-related symbols, up to max_records.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_dylibs_resolve
definition.description: Follow how the dynamic linker would find every library an app bundle's programs load: @executable_path, @loader_path and @rpath chains, load-once, weak links and architecture slices, with outcomes resolved, system, unresolved or undetermined and findings such as skipped-rpath-entry. Never follows links out of the bundle.

architecture.description: Architecture slice to follow; each entry program's preferred slice when omitted.

path.description: Absolute path of an app bundle (or a Mach-O inside one); the active target when omitted.

roots.description: Extra folders searched for absolute install names outside the bundle (like a system root).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_macho_show
definition.description: Header, architecture slices, every load command (libraries with versions, run paths, UUID, build versions, encryption, code-signature range, entry point, segments) plus a page of imports and exports of a Mach-O file or an app bundle's executable. Built-in parser; uses the active target unless path is given.

architecture.description: Slice of a universal binary (arm64, arm64e, x86_64, ...); arm64, then x86_64, then the first when omitted.

path.description: Absolute path of a Mach-O file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_nib_decode
definition.description: Decode compiled nib and storyboard files (NIB archives and keyed-archive nibs; .nib, .storyboardc and whole app bundles) into object graphs: objects with classes and values, outlet and action connections, and the view hierarchy. Bounded by max_documents, max_objects and max_connections.

path.description: Absolute path of a .nib file, .nib or .storyboardc folder, or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_objc_classes_list
definition.description: Deduplicated Objective-C class and category names (with method counts), optionally filtered by a substring.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: Only names containing this (case-insensitive); everything when empty.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_objc_protocols_list
definition.description: Objective-C protocols with their methods, plus Swift protocols from symbols.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_plist_show
definition.description: Read a property list (XML or binary) as normalised JSON: a .plist file, an app bundle's Info.plist, or the Info.plist embedded in a Mach-O executable. Uses the active target unless path is given.

path.description: Absolute path of a file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_signature_show
definition.description: Decode a Mach-O code signature: code directories (identifier, team id, flags, hash type, slot counts, cdhash), page and special-slot hashes re-computed and compared, requirements as text, entitlements, and whether a CMS signature is present. The CMS signature itself is not verified.

architecture.description: Slice of a universal binary (arm64, arm64e, x86_64, ...); arm64, then x86_64, then the first when omitted.

path.description: Absolute path of a Mach-O file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_slices_list
definition.description: List the architecture slices of a thin or universal Mach-O (CPU type and subtype, offset, size, alignment, file type).

path.description: Absolute path of a file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_swift_symbols_demangle
definition.description: Turn mangled Swift symbol names into readable declarations, in order, each marked demangled, unchanged (not a Swift name) or invalid. Built-in demangler; no target needed.

symbols.description: Mangled names, one per entry (1–10000; single line, no NUL).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_swift_types_list
definition.description: Swift symbols grouped into classes, structs, enums, protocols, extensions and other, by type path and role (accessor, descriptor, method...).

category.description: classes, structs, enums, protocols, extensions or other.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: Only type paths containing this (case-insensitive).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_ui_action_trace
definition.description: UI action or selector (e.g. `saveDocument:`) → handlers (Objective-C methods, matching names, code using the string) → the static calls they make, bounded by max_depth/max_nodes/max_edges. Best effort; limits are listed.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_image_generate
definition.description: Make a picture with fal.ai (Nano Banana Pro) and save it as a PNG inside app/: a texture, a sky or background, an icon, a title screen or concept art. shape: square (1024x1024, default), wide (1024x576) or tall (576x1024). Costs about $0.15, counted against the project's asset budget. Describe original designs in the original's style; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork. Returns where it was saved, the cost and the budget left.

prompt.description: What to draw, in detail (subject, style, colours, lighting).

save_as.description: Where to save it, relative to app/, ending in .png (e.g. Assets/Textures/crate.png).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_remove
definition.description: Remove an asset provider's stored key (`provider`, default fal).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_set
definition.description: Store an asset provider's key (`provider`, default fal) for generated pictures and 3D models in the system keychain (or the private key file). It's never shown again or written to logs.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_status
definition.description: Whether each asset provider (fal.ai today) has a key for generated pictures and 3D models, stored or in its environment variable. `stored` answers for `provider` (default fal). Keys themselves are never shown.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_model_generate
definition.description: Make a game-ready, low-poly 3D model (GLB) with fal.ai (Tripo P1) and save it inside app/. Give a prompt (a picture is made first, then turned into the model) or an image (a web address, or a picture inside the project such as reference/picture-1.png). faces caps the face count (48 to 20000, default 3000): about 500-1500 for small props and pickups, 2000-5000 for weapons, furniture and vehicles, 6000-15000 for main characters; fewer faces run faster, so use the fewest that still look right. textured (default true) gives colours and surfaces. A textured model costs $0.50 plus $0.15 for the picture, counted against the project's asset budget; it takes a minute or two. Describe one original object per model; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork. Returns where it was saved, the cost and the budget left.

faces.description: Most faces the model may have, 48 to 20000 (default 3000). Fewer faces run faster.

image.description: A picture to turn into the model: a web address, or a picture inside the project.

prompt.description: What to make: one object, described in detail. Used when no image is given.

save_as.description: Where to save it, relative to app/, ending in .glb (e.g. Assets/Models/crate.glb).

textured.description: Colours and surfaces (default true); false makes a plain grey model for $0.40 instead of $0.50.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_checklist
definition.description: Show the person your plan as a short checklist and keep it current: todos with content (a plain step), activeForm ("Drawing the map") and status (pending, in_progress or completed). Call it again whenever a step changes; the app pins it above the prompt box.

activeForm.description: What it says while doing it ("Drawing the map").

content.description: The step, in plain words.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_command_run
definition.description: Run a command in app/ (npm install, npm run build, cargo build, the game engine's build...) and return its exit code and the end of its output. Common build commands go ahead; dev servers and watchers are refused (they never exit); anything else asks the person. Default limit 10 minutes, at most 2 hours.

command.description: The command, run in app/ (`&&` joins steps).

timeout_secs.description: Time limit in seconds (default 600, at most 7200).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_edit
definition.description: Replace exact text in a file: old_text must appear exactly once (or set replace_all). Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

path.description: A file relative to the project.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_read
definition.description: Read a text file in the project (app/, capture/, reference/...), paged by lines with offset/limit for big files.

limit.description: How many lines (default: up to 256 KB).

path.description: A file relative to the project, e.g. `app/src/main.rs` or `capture/README.md`.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_write
definition.description: Create or replace a text file. Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

content.description: The whole new contents.

path.description: A file relative to the project, e.g. `app/src/main.rs`.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_files_list
definition.description: List files and folders in the project being built (default: app/), a few levels deep. Paths are relative to the project folder; build output and dependencies (node_modules, target, dist...) are skipped.

depth.description: How many levels down (default 4, at most 8).

path.description: A folder relative to the project (default `app`).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_archive_extract
definition.description: Extract every regular file of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR or ASAR (plus its .asar.unpacked files) into a fresh private temporary folder chosen by Craft Anything, and return its path. Bounded size and count; entries that would escape the folder are refused.

if_tampered.description: What to do when an ASAR integrity hash or ZIP CRC does not match.

path.description: Absolute path of the ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR or ASAR. Defaults to the active target.

oneOf.description: Stop with an error when a recorded hash or checksum does not match the content.
Record mismatches as contradictions and keep going.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_archive_show
definition.description: Content-addressed inventory of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR, Electron ASAR, app bundle or folder: every file with size, kind, role and sha256; nested archives opened to a bounded depth; ASAR integrity hashes and ZIP CRCs checked. Paged (offset/limit).
