pid.description: A running process to attach to instead of starting a program.

program.description: Absolute path of the program to start under the debugger.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_command_run
definition.description: Run one Rizin command line in a debug session (for example `dr` registers, `db main` breakpoint, `dc` continue, `ds` step, `dbt` backtrace, `dm` memory maps, `pd 10 @ rip`, `px 64 @ rsp`; chain with `;`) and return its output and any `ERROR:` lines, waiting up to timeout_seconds. A command still running at the deadline (a `dc` that never stops) keeps running and the next command waits for it. Visual mode isn't available. Commands can run the program and change its memory, so this asks for consent.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the command to finish: 1–300, default 10.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_end
definition.description: End a Rizin debug session: ask Rizin to quit (which ends a program it started; an attached process is detached), then stop it and anything it started.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_show
definition.description: Show one Rizin debug session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether Rizin is alive, what it debugs, whether a command is still running, and any output that arrived since the last command.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rust_binary_show
definition.description: Identify a Rust program (ELF, PE or Mach-O, or any file) from its bytes: rustc version strings and the toolchain commit from /rustc/<commit>/ paths, the standard-library path layout, crates with versions from embedded Cargo paths (registry/src/<index>/<crate>-<version>/ and git checkouts), the program's own source paths left by panic locations, well-known panic messages, Rust symbol names (legacy and v0 mangling) with demangled samples and whether they are stripped, and the cargo-auditable dependency list (.dep-v0) when present. Confidence is honest: strong signals (symbols, toolchain paths, dependency data) versus weak ones (panic text alone). Built-in; never runs the program.

path.description: Absolute path of the program; the active target when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_sections_list
definition.description: Segments and sections with address ranges, file offsets, permissions and entropy.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_source_folder_write
definition.description: Write each function of the active target as pseudo-C to its own file in a folder, across as many runs as it takes: running again with the same folder skips what's done and continues, and a state file records the target's SHA-256 (another target is refused) and each finished function. Each call stops at max_functions or max_seconds and says how far it got. Files are written atomically. Uses the built-in decompiler, as native_functions_decompile does. Refuses a folder with other files in it.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

folder.description: Absolute path of the folder to write to: new or empty, or one an earlier run of this tool wrote.

max_functions.description: Most functions to write in this call (1..=1000000, default 1000).

max_seconds.description: Stop starting new functions after this long (0..=3600, default 120).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_strings_browse
definition.description: Printable strings (ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16) in data sections with their addresses and how many places use them. Optional filters: one address, one section (`.rdata`); native_strings_find finds text. Paged.

address.description: Only the string at this address (0x-hex).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

section.description: Only strings in this section (`.rdata`, `__cstring`; case doesn't matter).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_strings_find
definition.description: Complete, deterministic search of the program's strings. mode literal or regex; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: What to look for.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_value_flow_show
definition.description: Register def-use graph of a function (which instruction's result each instruction reads), parameter uses and side effects, following callees to max_depth. Nodes are paged (offset/limit).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

function.description: Function name or address.

max_call_sites.description: Most call sites to examine (1..=4096, default 256).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_window_capture
definition.description: Start a program (an app or a game), wait for its window, take a picture of it and close the program (Windows and macOS). Optionally save the PNG to `output`, and the UI tree of its windows (as runtime_ui_read reads it; Windows and macOS) to `ui_tree` as JSON. It runs the program, so it needs consent.

output.description: Save the picture here as a PNG (an absolute path; its folder must exist).

program.description: The program to start (an absolute path).

ui_tree.description:
Also save the UI tree of its windows here as JSON, read just before it's closed (an
absolute path; its folder must exist). Windows and macOS.

wait_secs.description: Seconds to let it start and draw before the picture (default 8, at most 120).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_xrefs_list
definition.description: References to an address (calls, jumps, data, strings, pointers, imports) and the references made from it. Defaults to the cursor. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_capture_show
definition.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. Decodes Ethernet (VLAN), raw IP, Linux cooked and loopback links; IPv4, IPv6, TCP, UDP, ICMP. Each packet is decoded on its own: no stream reassembly, no decryption.

limit.description: Conversations per page (1–5000, default 100). Inventories show their top 100.

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_fields_show
definition.description: List decoded fields of individual packets in a saved pcap or pcapng capture, paged: frame number, time, link, protocol stack, addresses and ports, conversation (flow) id, IP TTL, TCP flags/sequence/window, UDP and ICMP details, DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x request or status line with Host, TLS ClientHello SNI/ALPN/versions. Filter by protocol (e.g. dns, tls, http, tcp, udp, icmp, ipv6, arp), IP address, port, or flow id from packets_capture_show. Built-in decoder.

flow.description: Only packets of this conversation (the flow id from packets_capture_show, e.g. 3 or "f3").

ip.description: Only packets from or to this IP address.

offset.description: First matching packet of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

port.description: Only packets from or to this TCP/UDP port.

protocol.description: Only packets with this protocol in their stack (eth, vlan, ipv4, ipv6, arp, tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, dns, mdns, http, tls).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_inventory_show
definition.description: Inventories of a saved pcap or pcapng capture: packet count, protocol stacks, IPv4/IPv6 addresses with packet counts, DNS questions and the addresses answered for them, TLS server names (SNI) and HTTP request URIs (credentials removed), each with counts and limited to `limit` rows. Uses Wireshark's tshark when installed (engine=auto or tshark; full dissectors, run with a deadline and capped output) and the built-in decoder otherwise (engine=built_in forces it).

limit.description: Rows kept per inventory, most frequent first (1–10000, default 100).

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

oneOf.description: tshark when installed, the built-in decoder otherwise.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_add
definition.description: Add an external MCP server as a plugin ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): an id, and either a command (a local server, with args, env and cwd) or a url (a remote https server, with headers). A plugin added here always asks before each call. replace overwrites a plugin with the same id. Run plugins_refresh next to read its tools.

command.description: The program of a local server.

headers.description: Sent with every request to a remote server (e.g. `Authorization`).

id.description: Toolset id and tool-id prefix: lower-case letters, digits and `_`.

name.description: The name people see (default: the id).

replace.description: Overwrite a plugin with the same id.

url.description: A remote server's address: `https://...`, or `http://` to this computer.

wasm.description:
A WASM component plugin's file (full path to a `.wasm`), instead of a command or url. Its
tools load from the next start, in a build with the `wasm-plugins` feature.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_list
definition.description: The external MCP servers configured as plugins ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): id, command, whether it's on and asks before each call, and the tools cached from its last refresh.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_refresh
definition.description: Start a plugin's MCP server (or every enabled one), read its tool list and cache it. New or changed tools are offered from the next start of the app or CLI. It runs the plugin's program, so it needs consent.

id.description: One plugin's id (default: every enabled plugin).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_remove
definition.description: Remove a plugin from config.toml by its id. Its tools stop being offered from the next start.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_assets_allow
definition.description: Turn on or off whether the builder may generate pictures and 3D models for a project (paid per asset from its asset budget, and only with an asset provider's key), or read it with no value. Off until the person turns it on.

allow.description: true lets the builder generate assets, false stops it; leave out to only read it.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_assets_budget
definition.description: Set what a project may spend on generated pictures and 3D models (US dollars), or read it with no amount. Shows what's been spent so far.

budget_usd.description: The new budget in US dollars (0 to 10 000); leave out to only read it.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_build_finish
definition.description: The person is happy with the build as it is (#210): its status becomes Ready and the conversation says they called it done, so a paused, stopped or failed build no longer offers to carry on. Everything so far is kept, and a new message carries on from here. It doesn't stop a build that is still running: pause it first.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_delete
definition.description: Delete a project: everything Craft Anything made in its folder (its records, checks, and what was built in app/). The person's own files stay (an app edited in place, the files a project started from). Can't be undone, so `confirm` must be true; stop a build first.

confirm.description: Must be true: deleting can't be undone.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_duplicate
definition.description: Copy a project beside it under a new name, to try something else from where it is: what was built, the pictures of the original and the study come along; the conversation, questions and usage don't, and neither do dependencies or compiler output (the next build makes them again). An app edited in place is copied into the copy's app/ folder.

name.description: The copy's name (default: "<name> copy").

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_inbox_answer
definition.description: Answer a question or approval a project is waiting on (an id from project_show): a choice or text for questions, allow (and always) for approvals. The answer reaches a running build at once and is kept in the project's conversation.

always.description: Allow this kind of action for the rest of the project (approvals).

text.description: A typed answer (questions), or a reason (approvals).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_list
definition.description: List the projects in every project folder from settings (where new projects go, then `project_folders`), or in one folder, newest first: name, folder, app folder, request, target, stack, status, the latest check and how many questions are waiting.

projects_dir.description: Only this folder (default: every project folder from settings).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_open_folder
definition.description: Open the project's folder (or its app/ folder) in the file manager, or one of its pinned builds' folders.

app.description: Open the app/ folder (what was built) instead of the project folder.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_create
definition.description: Keep the project's current build at hand to open later, whatever the builder changes next. `frozen` (the default) copies the app's files and its program into the project's pinned/ folder, without compiler output or dependencies it doesn't start from, so rebuilds can't change or break it. `light` copies the program and the code too but hard-links dependencies and media to the project's, saving their space: replacing or deleting those in the project leaves the pin's as they were, but a file rewritten in place changes in both. With `estimate`, only says what each would take. Websites can't be pinned yet.

estimate.description: Only say what each kind of copy would take; pin nothing.

mode.description:
`frozen` (default): a copy of its own; `light`: shares dependencies and media with the
project. `live` was retired and is refused.

name.description: Its name (default: the project's name and round).

PinMode.description: How a pin keeps its build.

oneOf.description: Its own copy of the build, which nothing else changes (the default).
Its own program and code, sharing dependencies and media with the project.

The project's app where it is, as the latest build left it. No longer made (it only
opened what Play opens); pins already saved this way still work.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_delete
definition.description: Remove a pin. Its copy goes with it, including anything the program saved beside itself there, so `confirm` must be true; a running pin is refused until it's stopped.

confirm.description: Must be true: a pin's copy, and what it saved, can't be brought back.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_open
definition.description: Start a pinned build in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true (copies of one pin share the files they save beside themselves). A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent.

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_rename
definition.description: Give a pin a new name.

name.description: Its new name.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_stop
definition.description: Close what a pin started in this session (every copy of it).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pins_list
definition.description: The pins of one project, or of every project in the project folders from settings: id, name, frozen or light, the round it was pinned at, its size, and whether it's running (started in this session).

project.description: Only this project's pins (default: every project's).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_plan_fold
definition.description: Fold the builder's plan card away (#504). The steps stay in the project's conversation, and a later run's plan shows again. Call it between builds: a build saves its conversation as it goes, so a fold made during one can be overwritten by that build's next save.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_play
definition.description: Start the finished game or app a project built (its program, a Unity or Unreal package, or a Godot project in Godot), in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true. A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent. Websites use project_preview instead. Known limit on Windows: when the caller's output is a pipe, the started program inherits it, so a caller reading that output to its end waits until the program exits (#207).

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_preview
definition.description: Serve a project's built website on this computer only (loopback) and return its address. It keeps serving for this session; with `wait`, the call itself serves until it's cancelled (Ctrl+C in the CLI).

wait.description: Serve until the call is cancelled instead of returning at once (for the CLI).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_questions_set
definition.description: Choose whether the builder's questions (core_person_ask) in a project are shown to the person to answer (`ask`) or answered with "decide yourself and say what you chose" (`decide`); `default` follows the app's setting (`questions` in settings, which follows Auto mode until set). With no mode, says what applies now. Takes effect from the builder's next question, also mid-build.

mode.description: `ask`, `decide` or `default`; none just reads what applies.

QuestionsChoice.description: What a project's questions should get.

oneOf.description: The app's setting.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_rename
definition.description: Give a project a new name (its folder stays where it is).

name.description: Its new name.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_show
definition.description: One project: its request, target, stack, status, checks, questions still waiting for an answer, and its conversation (paged with offset/limit, newest last).

limit.description: Return at most this many items (default and maximum 200; the newest when no offset).

offset.description: Skip this many conversation items from the start.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_decoders_list
definition.description: List the device protocols the installed rtl_433 can decode: number, name, and whether it runs by default (the others only run when asked for with decoders). Optional engine.

filter.description: Only decoders whose name contains this text (any case).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_recording_decode
definition.description: Decode a saved radio recording (absolute path or the active target) with rtl_433: I/Q samples (.cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32) or demodulated AM/FM (.am.s16, .fm.s16), format and sample rate read from the file name (for example g001_433.92M_250k.cu8; 250 kHz when absent) unless sample_rate is given. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus counts by model. decoders limits decoding to those protocol numbers (see radio_decoders_list); otherwise rtl_433's default set runs. Optional engine.

decoders.description: Protocol numbers to decode (from radio_decoders_list); empty runs the default set.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording; omit to use the active target.

sample_rate.description: Sample rate in Hz, when the file name doesn't say.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_activity_show
definition.description: What a project's builds did, line by line, newest last: each stage, every command and file the builder touched and how it ended, what it said, and what programs printed outside the conversation. Secrets are hidden. Works while a build runs and after. `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 2000), `offset` lines back from the newest.

limit.description: How many lines to return (200 by default, at most 2000).

offset.description: How many lines back from the newest to end at (0 by default).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_check
definition.description: For the builder: test the project's current build against the original now, with the same checks Craft Anything runs after each turn (a website's likeness at each width with the padding, colour, font and layout differences; an app's or game's picture against the original's; whether it builds; the mechanics sheet; credits). The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it lists and check again before replying. Not counted as a round. project defaults to the project this tool server works for.

project.description: The project's folder; default: the project this tool server was started for.

wait_minutes.description:
Longest wait for the result, in minutes (1..=60, default 20): a website with several pages
or a game's engine build takes a few minutes.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note
definition.description: Tell a running build something more; the agent reads it at its next step. With no build running, start a follow-up with rebuild_start instead.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note_withdraw
definition.description: Take back a note given with rebuild_note (by the id it returned) while the agent hasn't read it yet; it returns the note's text. Once the agent has read it, it can't be taken back.

id.description: The note's id, as rebuild_note returned it.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_question_ask
definition.description: Ask a question about a project's build ("where are the latest files?", "why this engine?") without starting a build or a round, and without changing anything. Claude Code answers from a copy of the builder's own session, which isn't kept, reading files only (none in Clean room); an AI with an API key answers with the tools that change nothing. Other coding agents are refused. Safe while a build runs: it doesn't interrupt it. Returns the answer, how it was answered and its cost, and keeps it in the project (`rebuild_questions_list`).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_questions_list
definition.description: The questions asked about a project's build and their answers, oldest first (the newest 200).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_start
definition.description: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start on their own as others finish. It runs a coding agent that writes and builds code, so it needs consent.

backend.description:
The coding agent to use (a backend name), kept with a new project for its later changes;
default: the one set up for building.

build_with.description: What to build with: an engine (unity, unreal, godot, rust) or a stack's full name.

existing.description:
With `project_folder` that has files: `edit` (they're the app, edited in place) or
`start_from` (material to start from; the app is built in app/ beside them).

generate_assets.description:
For a new game: the builder may generate pictures and 3D models (paid from the person's
asset provider key, within the project's budget). Default false; change it later with
project_assets_allow.

pictures.description:
Pictures of the original (absolute paths): the look the person expects. They're copied
into the project's reference/ folder for the builder.

project.description: Continue this project folder instead of starting a new one.

project_folder.description:
Start the new project in this folder itself instead (it's added to the project list). If
it already has files, `existing` says what they are.

projects_dir.description: Where a new project's folder goes (default: the projects folder from settings).

request.description: What to make (a new project), or the follow-up message (with `project`).

resume.description:
With `project`: carry on where its last run stopped (paused, or the app or the computer
stopped) instead of sending `request` as a follow-up.

rounds.description: Refinement rounds after the first build (default 2).

target.description: For a new project: a web address, an absolute path to an app, game or file, or `-` for none.

ExistingFiles.description: What the files already in a picked folder are to a new project.

oneOf.description: The app itself: the builder edits them in place.
Material to start from: the builder reads them and builds the app in app/ beside them.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_status
definition.description: Whether a project's build is running in this session (or queued, and where), its status and note, the latest check, and how many questions are waiting.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_stop
definition.description: Pause a project's running build. Its work so far is kept; a follow-up continues it.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_captures_compare
definition.description: Compare two runtime_walkthrough_record evidence records dimension by dimension (terminal, exit, filesystem, events) and report what changed. Pure; no program is run.

left.description: The first run: runtime_walkthrough_record evidence (inline, {"kind":"saved",...} or a bare id).

right.description: The second run, in the same forms.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_read
definition.description: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters. Other hosts get a clear wrong_os result.

max_nodes.description: Largest number of accessibility nodes to return.

pid.description: The process id of the running app.

screenshot.description: Include a screenshot (PNG, base64) alongside the tree.

window_id.description: A specific window to restrict to (on Windows, its window handle).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_walkthrough_record
definition.description: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Each step names an action and an element (its exact title or identifier). macOS: any accessibility action (e.g. AXPress). Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. Each step reports dispatched, element_not_found, not_supported, unknown_action or failed. Password fields' titles and values are never read. Other hosts get wrong_os.

steps.description: Steps to perform, each an accessibility action such as press/focus on an element path.

action.description:
Accessibility action, e.g. `AXPress` (on Windows also press, expand, collapse, toggle,
select or focus).

element.description: Identifier or title path to the element the action targets.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
definition.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

environment.description: Extra environment variables applied on top of the inherited environment.

executable.description: The program to run (absolute path or a name resolved on PATH).

finish_ms.description: 0 = SIGKILL at the deadline; > 0 = SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

normalization.description:
Make two runs comparable: replace values that change every run (on by default for process
ids, ports and 10 ms time buckets).

sandbox.description: Run inside bubblewrap if it is installed (recorded honestly either way).

watched_paths.description:
Absolute paths to snapshot before and after (opt-in). File contents are never read; only
path, size and sha256.

working_directory.description: Working directory (absolute). Defaults to the program's own default.

data.description: Text to type. A trailing newline is not added for you.

paths.description: Replace the working directory and the temp folder with <cwd> and <tmp>.

patterns.description: Literal replacements (no patterns), applied last; at most 100.

pids.description: Replace the run's process ids with <pid>.

ports.description: Replace ports after localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and [::1] with <port>.

time_step_ms.description: Round event dispatch times down to this many milliseconds (0 keeps them exact).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_set
definition.description: Set one setting by its dotted key from settings_show (`auto_mode`, `deep_mode`, `projects_dir`, `assets.budget_usd`...) to a JSON value, then save. Unknown keys and values of the wrong type are refused, and nothing is written.

key.description: A dotted key from settings_show, e.g. `deep_mode`.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_show
definition.description: The current settings as JSON (mode, Auto mode, Deep mode/Ghidra, engine paths, projects folder, asset budget and picture model, AI backends). API keys are never in settings.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_apply
definition.description: Connect Craft Anything to coding-agent apps: register its MCP server in their config files (backing each up first) and install the skill. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_doctor
definition.description: Check the install, each agent app's registration, engines, and that the MCP server answers.

clients.description: Only these clients; empty checks every detected one.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_plan
definition.description: What connecting Craft Anything to coding-agent apps (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...) would change: each config file, the lines that change, and the skill files. Writes nothing.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_uninstall
definition.description: Remove Craft Anything's entries and skill from every agent app's config. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_browser_connect
definition.description: Attach to a loopback CDP endpoint (a browser started with --remote-debugging-port) or launch a located Chromium headless, and report the product, protocol version and debuggable target count. A quick connectivity check before the other browser tools.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback CDP endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9222. Omit to launch a browser.

launch.description: Launch a located Chromium when no endpoint is given.

no_sandbox.description: Pass --no-sandbox when launching (needed in some containers).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_coverage_measure
definition.description: Turn on V8 precise coverage on one page, observe for a window, then report per-script which functions and block ranges ran (UTF-16 offsets, with call counts when available). Changes the page's profiler state and discards coverage data on stop, so it is not idempotent.

offset.description: First script of the page in the result.

watch_ms.description: How long to let code run while measuring (milliseconds, default 10s).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_listeners_list
definition.description: Resolve a CSS selector on one page and list the DOM event listeners registered on that element: event type, capture/passive/once flags and the handler's script location (URL, line, column). No handler source is read.

selector.description: A CSS selector identifying the element.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_mcp_tools_list
definition.description: Best effort: enable the experimental WebMCP CDP domain and collect any tools the page advertises (names and declared input outlines only) during a short window. The tools are never invoked. Honest when the browser does not support the domain.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_modules_trace
definition.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded and build their ES module import graph: each script and the specifiers it imports, resolved to URLs where relative, with bare specifiers reported as needing an import map. Static reading of the live sources; nothing is executed.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_js_analyze
definition.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded over CDP and run the built-in JavaScript analyser on them: chunk graph, module boundaries, routes, HTTP endpoints and vendor fingerprints. Optionally decodes inline (data:) source maps and fetches same-origin maps. Passive; nothing is executed.

load_source_maps.description: Decode inline (data:) source maps and fetch same-origin maps.

offset.description: First module of the page in the result.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_screenshot_take
definition.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current state of one page and return it inline with its sha256 (plus bytes, dimensions, base64). Passive; the page is not navigated.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_show
definition.description: Passively observe one page over CDP for a short window: frame origins, a DOM summary (node names/types and attribute names with value lengths only), parsed scripts (optionally their sources, each with its sha256), resources, and — each opt-in — accessibility names, console entries, network request outlines, WebSocket outlines and storage key names. Never navigates, clicks or evaluates. Cookies, auth headers and storage values are never kept; JSON bodies become outlines.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (any encoding). Only the count is recorded.

target_id.description: The target id to inspect (from web_pages_list); the first page otherwise.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_states_capture
definition.description: On the open website, open up to max_states of its visible menus, pop-ups, tabs and collapsed sections (aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, unselected tabs, <summary>; never form controls or submit buttons) one at a time: click it, take a screenshot, record what changed (expanded, a dialog appeared, the tab or the address changed), then put the page back. Writes state-<n>.png and states.json into a new folder. Clicking runs the site's own code, so it needs your approval.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the states are written there.

width.description: Page width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_watch
definition.description: Passively watch one page over a longer window (default 10s) and record a bounded timeline of network request outlines, console entries, WebSocket frame outlines and navigation/lifecycle events, all data-minimised. Never navigates or evaluates.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pages_list
definition.description: List the debuggable targets (pages, workers, iframes) of a loopback CDP endpoint with their ids, kinds and origin-only URLs, plus the browser product and protocol version. Read-only discovery over HTTP; no WebSocket.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pixels_compare
definition.description: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

before.description: Earlier PNG: a web_page_screenshot_take evidence (inline/retained), or inline {base64} / {path}.

common_area.description:
Compare the area both images share (top-left) when their sizes differ, and add a coarse
`layout_similarity` (0..1, share of 16 px tiles with matching mean colour) and a
`perceptual_similarity` (0..1, mean SSIM of brightness: edges, text, texture). Use it to
compare a rebuild with the original page, whose heights rarely match exactly.

ignore.description:
With common_area: a noise-<width>.png mask from web_site_capture ({path} or {base64});
its white squares (parts that change by themselves) are left out of the layout and detail.

tolerance.description: Per-channel difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed (0..=255).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_recording_show
definition.description: Read a HAR capture offline: requests, methods, statuses, hosts, timings and an API surface grouped by method + origin + path template, with JSON bodies reduced to outlines (no values). Cookies, credential headers, URL user-info and credential-like query values are never kept; secrets the caller names are redacted in raw, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms. Paged (offset/limit) or pick entries with record_numbers.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (tokens, emails, ids). Only their count is recorded.

path.description: Absolute path of the capture file.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_scripts_save
definition.description: Write the scripts held by a web capture (page inspection or walkthrough evidence, a capture JSON file, or a HAR with saved bodies) into a new folder as files/<host>/<path> plus manifest.json; query variants and collisions get content-hash names with a stated reason. The result names the folder to pass to js_app_map.

capture.description: Capture evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) whose result lists scripts with url and source.

capture_path.description: Or an absolute path to a capture JSON file or a HAR file.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_capture
definition.description: Record the open website into a new folder: full-page PNG screenshots at each requested width, the rendered HTML, design tokens (fonts, sizes, weights, text and background colours as hex, radii, shadows, spacing, content widths, CSS custom properties), the widths its CSS switches layout at, the layout at each width (page width, heading and text sizes, each section's padding, gap, content column and items per row), a layout outline of visible landmarks, headings, controls and images with positions, asset lists (images, stylesheets, scripts, font files, the requests it made), links and form outlines (never values). Writes capture.json and a README.md summary.

max_height.description: Tallest screenshot in CSS pixels; longer pages are cut here (600..=20000, default 12000).

noise_pass.description:
Photograph each width a second time a moment later and save the parts that changed by
themselves (carousels, videos, animations) as noise-<width>.png, white where it changed,
so comparisons can leave them out (default false).

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the capture is written there.

widths.description: Page widths to screenshot, in CSS pixels (1..=4 widths, each 320..=3840). Default: desktop and phone.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_close
definition.description: Close the private browser started by web_site_open and delete its temporary profile.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_open
definition.description: Load a web page (http/https) in a private browser owned by this session (fresh profile, no history or logins) at a chosen window size, wait for it to finish loading, and report its final address, title and size. Every browser tool then inspects this page unless given another endpoint. Runs the site's scripts, so it needs your approval.

headless.description: Run the browser without a window (default true).

height.description: Window height in CSS pixels (320..=4000, default 900).

settle_ms.description: Extra time to let late content settle after the load event, in milliseconds (default 2000).

url.description: The page to open (http or https).

width.description: Window width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_snapshots_compare
definition.description: Compare two web_page_show captures (frame origins, elements, resources, endpoints and script URLs added or removed), or two web_walkthrough_record runs step by step (steps aligned by step_id, then position: action, status, URL, error and artifact changes; network requests; event counts). normalization lists plain text replacements (e.g. a build id) applied to both sides first. Pure computation over evidence; no browser.

before.description: The earlier capture: web_page_show / web_page_watch evidence (inline or retained).

normalization.description:
Exact-literal replacements applied to every text value of both sides before comparing, in
rule_id order (at most 100), so volatile values such as build ids don't count as changes.

match.description: The exact text to replace (no patterns).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_build
definition.description: Read a network recording (.har) of the original site and write standin.json into a folder: its routes (method and path template, with ids as {id}), and for each the status codes, content types, query names and a bounded set of recorded answers. It's for giving a rebuilt front end something to talk to. Credential headers, cookies and secret-shaped values are dropped and counted; pages, scripts and pictures are left out unless include_static is set. It only knows what was recorded. Returns a summary and a page of routes.

hidden_values.description: Values to drop wherever they appear, in every encoding (emails, ids, tokens). Only their count is recorded.

include_static.description: Also keep pages, scripts, styles, pictures, fonts and media.

only_hosts.description: Only these hosts, e.g. api.example.com (or with a port). Default: every host.

output_dir.description: Absolute path of the folder to write standin.json in (made if missing). An earlier stand-in there is replaced.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording (.har).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_show
definition.description: List the stand-ins running in this session with the requests they answered, and page through the requests that had no recorded answer, most asked first, each with why and the nearest recorded routes. This is how a builder finds out what its front end needs that the recording doesn't have.

id.description: Only this stand-in. Default: every one running.

limit.description: Requests with no answer per page (1–1000).

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_start
definition.description: Answer HTTP requests on this computer from a file written by web_standin_build, and return its URL to point a rebuilt front end at. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, refuses requests addressed to any other host and pages from other computers, and allows local pages through CORS. Stays running for this session, or until web_standin_stop. A request with no recorded answer gets a 404 with the nearest routes as JSON. Writes replay what was recorded and change nothing. Runs no code from the recording.

path.description: Absolute path of a file written by web_standin_build, or the folder holding it.

port.description: The port to listen on. 0 (the default) picks a free one.

wait.description:
Keep this call going until it's cancelled, then stop and say what was answered. For a one-off
command line, whose session would otherwise end and take the stand-in with it. No other tool
can run in this session meanwhile.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_stop
definition.description: Stop a stand-in started by web_standin_start and free its port: by id, or all of them. With neither, stops the only one running. Returns what it answered.

all.description: Stop every stand-in in this session.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_walkthrough_check
definition.description: Check a script for web_walkthrough_record without running a browser, and list every problem with the step it's in: unknown step kinds, missing fields, selectors CSS doesn't have (XPath, :has-text and the like), locators that aren't exactly one of selector, test_id or role with name, bad settings. Errors are what the recorder would refuse, by the same rules; warnings are what it would run but probably not as meant (a misspelt field it ignores, a repeated step_id). Touches no target.

script.description: What you'd pass to web_walkthrough_record, or only its list of actions.

definition.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_walkthrough_record
definition.description: Run a scripted browser session (goto/click/fill/press/select/wait; elements by CSS selector, test_id, or role and accessible name; optional step_id per step) over CDP, attaching to a loopback endpoint or launching a located Chromium. A fixed environment (viewport, locale, time zone, colour scheme, reduced motion, service workers; 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light by default) makes runs repeatable. Captures per-step network request outlines and optional screenshots; keep_bodies can also keep request/response bodies and header values (off by default, credentials and declared secrets redacted). storage can start the run with cookies and local/session storage (values treated as secrets). capture records screenshot, DOM, accessibility tree, history and storage key names after each step and/or at the end. capture.events records console, page errors, WebSockets, frames, workers, popups and (blocked) downloads, each tagged with its step. Executes page interactions and accesses the network, so it needs your approval; declared secrets are redacted in every encoding and bodies are reduced to outlines.

actions.description: The scripted actions, run in order (1..=200).

capture.description: What to record after each step and at the end of the run (besides each step's URL).

capture_network.description: Record network request outlines during the run.

environment.description: Fixed browser settings for the run, so two runs of the same steps see the same page.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear, in every encoding.

keep_bodies.description: Network content to keep besides request outlines (all off by default; needs capture_network).

launch.description: Launch a located Chromium (default when no endpoint is given).

screenshot_each_step.description: Capture a screenshot after each step.

storage.description:
Cookies and storage to start with (e.g. to explore the signed-in side of your own site).
Every value given here is treated as a secret and redacted wherever it shows up.

oneOf.description: The page's HTML, secrets redacted (256 KiB per step, 1 MiB at the end).
Roles and names, as a screen reader sees the page.
The tab's navigation history.
local/session storage key names and cookie names for the current origin (never values).
Console messages (text redacted, capped).
Uncaught exceptions on the page.
WebSocket connections and frames (text frames redacted, capped).
Frames attached, navigated and detached.
Web, shared and service workers started and stopped.
Windows the page opened.
Downloads the page started (they are blocked, never saved).

NetworkContent.description:
Which network values a run keeps. Kept text has declared secrets redacted; credential headers
are always redacted.

url.description: The http(s) URL the cookie belongs to.

events.description: Event families to record over the run, each event tagged with the step it happened in.

WalkthroughEnvironment.description: Viewport, locale, time zone and media settings applied before the first step.

bypass_service_workers.description: Requests skip service workers, so an offline cache can't hide the network.

reduced_motion.description: Ask pages to reduce motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

timezone.description: IANA time zone, e.g. UTC or Europe/Berlin.

WalkthroughStep.description: One scripted step: an action and, optionally, your name for it (echoed in the result).

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

definition.name: NotebookEdit
definition.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

notebook_path.description: The absolute path to the Jupyter notebook file to edit (must be absolute, not relative)

cell_id.description: The ID of the cell to edit. When inserting a new cell, the new cell will be inserted after the cell with this ID, or at the beginning if not specified.

new_source.description: The new source for the cell

cell_type.description: The type of the cell (code or markdown). If not specified, it defaults to the current cell type. If using edit_mode=insert, this is required.

edit_mode.description: The type of edit to make (replace, insert, delete). Defaults to replace.

Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents

Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 28800000ms / 480 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 14400000ms (240 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: TaskCreate
tools.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks
